reason: Attacked hardest, because the verifier admitted it had never opened the translation, and it still survives. Using Internet Archive full-text search across the scanned copies of Colquhoun’s English Leopard (Pantheon 1960, Collins/Fontana, Time reading edition, and others) the passage returns verbatim in every copy: "Unless we ourselves take a hand now, they’ll foist a republic on us. If we want things to stay as they are, things will have to change." So the wording is the named translation’s, not the Waldman 2007 rendering ("if we want everything to stay as it is, everything must change"), and not a later paraphrase. The locator holds too. The contents pages of those same scans read "1 Introduction to the Prince", "2 Donnafugata", "3 The Troubles of Don Fabrizio" and so on, so the divisions are numbered chapters with titles, as the note says; the chapter-one argument line runs "Rosary and introduction to the Prince . The garden and the dead soldier . Royal audiences . Dinner . A carriage to Palermo . Going to Mariannina’s . Conversation with Tancredi . In the office; estates and politics", which puts the talk with Tancredi inside chapter 1. Cross-check on the page: the Fontana contents give chapter I at p. 11 and chapter II at p. 45, and the p. 29 that the reference works cite for this sentence falls inside chapter 1, which corroborates the chapter and shows the proposed p. 19 was the bad reading; dropping the page was right. Speaker confirmed as Tancredi, and a secondary work quotes the sentence as "Lampedusa’s youthful Tancredi". Novel 1958, translation 1960, both pre-1999; nothing needing a warning. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, Lampedusa 0 of 3, not banned, no second Lampedusa in the August files. Tag Fiction. Source line 108 characters, name first, speaker in parentheses after the locator, translation last, no dash. One improvement only, offered below: the chapter has a title and the source has room for it.
